title: VAOM seeded cases
description: Known-error cases planted into a review queue to measure whether oversight works (VAOM v5 Readiness Condition 6, scorecard metric 9), as aviation screening projects fictional threats into baggage images. Human-approved and versioned. Planting follows Condition 6 and is enforced in code: only on matrix rows that enable seeding (which the matrix allows only where records feed no regulatory reporting, investigations or decisions about identifiable individuals); a planted case is marked as seeded in the Guardian's store, never becomes a decision record, can never execute whatever the reviewer does, and so never reaches a cap, the decision history or a calibration sample; reviewers are told that planting exists and at what rate, never which cases are planted. A seed is placed exactly as a real call would be, so it shows the reviewer what a real ask would show. Passing this schema is necessary but not sufficient: the seeds linter checks each seed against the matrix and binding. Draft 0.1.

approval.description: Sign-off by the role accountable for oversight of these decision types.

disclosure.description: Evidence that reviewers were told planting exists and at what rate. The approval page also says so on every visit.

row.description: The matrix row whose review queue the seed is planted in. The row must enable seeding.

tool.description: The host tool the seed poses as calling. The binding must map it to a capability of the row.

arguments.description: The call's arguments, as the reviewer will see them.

copy.description: Top-level argument names whose values are copied from the real call the seed is planted beside (an incident id, say), so the seed fits the work in progress.

error.description: The known error a reviewer should catch. Shown to the reviewer after they decide, never before.
